newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Benpres seen on target for 25 pct profit rise.
newsitem.headline: Benpres seen on target for 25 pct profit rise.

text.p: Benpres Holdings Corp on Monday announced unaudited net income of 1.82 billion pesos ($692 million) in 1996, but analysts said the final figure should reach two billion pesos.

In a disclosure to the Philippine Stock Exchange, Benpres said the figure did not include net earnings of subsidiaries for December 1996. It also did not include October-to-December earnings of Manila Electric Co (Meralco) and PCIBank, companies in which Benpres holds stakes.
The diversified holdings firm's unaudited figures represent a 12 percent increase over 1995's net income of 1.616 billion pesos.

"But even with the unaudited figures, we are fairly comfortable that we will meet our 25 percent earnings growth target or a net income of two billion pesos for all of 1996," Rafael L. Andrada, Benpres vice-president for finance, told Reuters.
"It (the 1.82 billion pesos) is not our full net income because the affiliates have yet to submit to their respective boards their earnings for the last month of 1996," Andrada added.
He said the incomplete figures were submitted to the stock exchange to meet the bourse's schedule for submission of income statements.

Noel Reyes, research head at Anscor Hagedorn Securities Inc, said the combined fourth-quarter incomes of PCIBank and Meralco could easily contribute 110 million to 130 million pesos to Benpres's bottom line for 1996.

"Meralco posted a strong sales volume growth for the last quarter while PCIBank is a pretty solid company, so it's likely that Benpres will attain its 25 percent target," said Joel Santillan, research head at Asia Merit Securities.
Meralco has already reported a 12.2 percent increase in sales volume for all of 1996 compared to the previous year. The company was previously expecting eight to 10 percent sales growth.

"The figures are within expectations and Benpres has been consistent in meeting its targets," said Cilette Liboro, research head at Citisecurities Inc. She added that television station ABS-CBN remained the biggest contributor to Benpres's earnings.
Benpres has 1.72 percent direct ownership in Meralco. The utility's biggest shareholder is First Philippine Holdings Corp, in which Benpres has a 26.59 percent stake.
In PCIBank, Benpres has a participating interest of 17.74 percent.
A Reuters poll of eight brokerage houses in late January showed that Benpres was expected to make 2.02 billion pesos in profit in 1996 up 25 percent from 1.616 billion pesos in 1995.
Benpres's Andrada said he expected 1997 earnings to grow a minimum 25 percent.

Santillan said Rockwell Land Corp may start contributing to the holding company's bottom line next year. Rockwell Land is the vehicle for the conversion of 15.5 hectares in Manila's financial district of Makati into a mixed-use commercial and residential centre.
Other subsidiaries of Benpres include international gateway facility and local exchange operator ICC Telecoms and cable operator Sky Vision Corp.
Analysts said that with ICC Telecoms' roll-out programme for 300,000 landlines on schedule, the unit may start contributing to the holding firm's earnings by the end of the year. ($1 = 26.3 pesos)
